raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Closes #43931.

`SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY` is still registered in `environ.py` and referenced from the speculative decoding docs, but nothing consumes it anymore. NGRAM verify read the flag in `ngram_info.py` back in #13153; the read was lost when NGRAM verify moved onto the shared `eagle_sample()` helper, so setting the env var today has no effect.

## Modifications

- `eagle_sample()` gains a keyword-only `force_greedy_verify` (default `False`); when set, the greedy predicate treats the batch as all-greedy.
- The NGRAM call site passes `envs.SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY.get()`. EAGLE and the other callers keep the default, so their acceptance behavior is unchanged.
- New unit test `test_ngram_force_greedy_verify.py` pins the plumbing at the predicate seam: flag on forces the greedy branch for a mixed batch, flag off preserves batch semantics, an already all-greedy batch is unaffected either way.

## Accuracy Tests

Default-path behavior is unchanged when the flag is unset; with the flag set, NGRAM verify selects the existing greedy branch instead of the sampling one. No GPU on this machine, so I ran the new unit test on CPU (3 passed) and left end-to-end output comparison to CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: one env lookup per NGRAM verify call, no kernel or hot-path changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (ruff check with the repo's selected rules + ruff format)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (not needed: the docs already describe the flag, this change makes the code match them)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, see above)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Merged current main and pushed `7bfe9851ff`. The conflict was in the shared verify signature: the resolution keeps both the existing `force_greedy_verify` override and the newer simulated acceptance-length / compact top-k parameters, rather than dropping either side. The NGRAM call chain and environment descriptor are unchanged.

Validation on the merged head: `test_ngram_force_greedy_verify.py` 3/3, a signature check confirms all four parameters are present, and changed-file pre-commit passes. An additional post-verify graph test did not get past collection because this local environment lacks `mlx`, so I am not counting it as validation. No GPU run.

Re-checked the flag semantics and its conventions against `Envs`, since this is the one thing that could make the fix wrong even when the wiring is right.

`SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY = EnvBool(False)` is already registered in `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`, and this PR does not add or rename a key. It reads the value through `envs.SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY.get()`, so no raw `os.getenv` or `os.environ` enters the path. Opt-in default, boolean typed, existing name kept.

The behaviour is the one the name claims: `_verify_uses_greedy` decides whether verify commits argmax rather than taking the sampling path, and this folds the flag into that predicate as `sampling_info.is_all_greedy or force_greedy_verify`. EAGLE callers never pass the kwarg, so they keep the default `False` and their predicate is byte-for-byte the old one.

Two small things I am flagging rather than hiding. The folded value goes into the `is_all_greedy` parameter, so that parameter now means "the schedule is greedy or the operator forced it"; if anyone would rather see a separate `force_greedy` argument on `_verify_uses_greedy` I am happy to widen it. And the helper's docstring still says "Whether EAGLE verify must commit argmax", which was already stale once NGRAM started reaching it through the shared `eagle_sample` helper, not something this PR introduces; I left it alone to keep the diff to the wiring.

The test pins the plumbing at the predicate seam rather than asserting a kernel outcome, which is the part that regressed, and it registers CPU CI through `register_cpu_ci` so it runs without a GPU.

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+"""The NGRAM greedy-verify flag must reach the verify branch predicate.
+
+SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY stayed registered and documented, but the
+NGRAM refactor onto the shared eagle_sample helper dropped the read: the
+greedy predicate only saw sampling_info.is_all_greedy. eagle_sample takes a
+force_greedy_verify override that the NGRAM worker feeds from the flag, so
+these tests pin the plumbing at the predicate seam. EAGLE callers never pass
+it and are unchanged.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.speculative import eagle_utils
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _PredicateHit(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def _capture_predicate_kwargs(monkeypatch, *, is_all_greedy, force_greedy_verify):
+    captured = {}
+
+    def spy(**kwargs):
+        captured.update(kwargs)
+        raise _PredicateHit
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(eagle_utils, "_verify_uses_greedy", spy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        eagle_utils,
+        "get_spec",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(speculative_use_rejection_sampling=False),
+    )
+
+    bs, draft_token_num, vocab = 1, 2, 16
+    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+        device=torch.device("cpu"),
+        forward_mode=SimpleNamespace(is_idle=lambda: False),
+        seq_lens=[4],
+        sampling_info=SimpleNamespace(
+            is_all_greedy=is_all_greedy,
+            acc_additive_penalties=None,
+            acc_scaling_penalties=None,
+            logit_bias=None,
+            has_watermark_candidates=False,
+        ),
+    )
+    verify_input = SimpleNamespace(
+        draft_token=torch.zeros(bs * draft_token_num, dtype=torch.int64),
+        draft_token_num=draft_token_num,
+        max_tree_depth=3,
+    )
+    logits_output = SimpleNamespace(
+        next_token_logits=torch.zeros(bs * draft_token_num, vocab)
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(_PredicateHit):
+        eagle_utils.eagle_sample(
+            verify_input,
+            batch,
+            logits_output,
+            force_greedy_verify=force_greedy_verify,
+        )
+    return captured
+
+
+def test_force_greedy_verify_reaches_predicate(monkeypatch):
+    captured = _capture_predicate_kwargs(
+        monkeypatch, is_all_greedy=False, force_greedy_verify=True
+    )
+    assert captured["is_all_greedy"] is True
+
+
+def test_default_keeps_sampling_predicate(monkeypatch):
+    captured = _capture_predicate_kwargs(
+        monkeypatch, is_all_greedy=False, force_greedy_verify=False
+    )
+    assert captured["is_all_greedy"] is False
+
+
+def test_all_greedy_batch_unaffected_by_default(monkeypatch):
+    captured = _capture_predicate_kwargs(
+        monkeypatch, is_all_greedy=True, force_greedy_verify=False
+    )
+    assert captured["is_all_greedy"] is True
